/-!
# Erdős Problem 572

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/572](https://www.erdosproblems.com/572)
- [Er64c] Erdős, P., Extremal problems in graph theory. Theory of Graphs and its
  Applications (1964), 29-36.
- [BoSi74] Bondy, J. A. and Simonovits, M., Cycles of even length in graphs.
  J. Combin. Theory Ser. B (1974), 97-105.
- [LUW95] Lazebnik, F., Ustimenko, V. A. and Woldar, A. J., A new series of dense graphs
  of high girth. Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. (N.S.) (1995), 73-79.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter

namespace Erdos572

/--
Show that for $k\geq 3$
$$\mathrm{ex}(n;C_{2k})\gg n^{1+\frac{1}{k}}.$$

This problem is #46 in Extremal Graph Theory in the graphs problem collection.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_572 (k : ℕ) (hk : 3 ≤ k) :
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in atTop,
      c * (n : ℝ) ^ (1 + 1 / (k : ℝ)) ≤
        (SimpleGraph.extremalNumber n (SimpleGraph.cycleGraph (2 * k)) : ℝ) := by
  sorry

-- TODO: Add variants of the problem.

end Erdos572

reformulations.difference: The Lean statement follows erdosproblems.com and asserts the bound for every k ≥ 3. The graphs problem collection entry it also cites (#46 in Extremal Graph Theory, Chung–Graham) poses Erdős's conjecture only for k = 4 and k ≥ 6: "Prove that t(n, C_{2k}) ≥ c n^{1+1/k} for k = 4 and k ≥ 6". The Lean also writes out `≫` as `∃ c > 0, ∀ᶠ n in atTop, c * n^(1+1/k) ≤ ex(n; C_{2k})`, with c chosen after k is fixed.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The cases k = 3 and k = 5 are theorems of Benson (1966), as erdosproblems.com notes ("Benson has proved this conjecture for k=3 and k=5"). Benson's girth-8 and girth-12 incidence graphs of generalized quadrangles and hexagons are C_6-free and C_10-free, with Θ(n^{4/3}) and Θ(n^{6/5}) edges. Monotonicity of ex(n;H) in n and the density of prime powers extend this to all large n. Füredi–Simonovits (arXiv 1306.5167, Corollary co:8) list ex(n,C_6)=Θ(n^{4/3}) and ex(n,C_10)=Θ(n^{6/5}) as known. So '∀ k ≥ 3' and '∀ k ∈ {4} ∪ [6,∞)' have the same truth value. The unfolding of ≫ is the standard Vinogradov meaning. The implied constant may depend on k, matching the Füredi–Simonovits form 'ex(n,C_{2k}) ≥ c_k n^{1+1/k}'. 'Eventually' is the only sensible reading, since ex(1;C_{2k}) = 0 < 1 = 1^{1+1/k}. It is also equivalent to 'for all n ≥ 2' after shrinking c, because ex(n;C_{2k}) ≥ 1 for n ≥ 2.

review.notes:
The file has a single declaration, `Erdos572.erdos_572`. It states exactly what erdosproblems.com/572 poses: for k ≥ 3, ex(n;C_{2k}) ≫ n^{1+1/k}. The quantifiers are in the right order (c depends on k), the inequality points the right way (a lower bound on ex), the constant c is present, and the bound is 'eventually', not 'for all n'. Lean checks in /workspace/review:
- With `pp.explicit`, the power elaborates to `HPow ℝ ℝ ℝ` via `Real.instPow` (rpow). The base (n:ℝ) is ≥ 0 and the exponent is 1 + 1/k with k ≥ 3, so there is no x/0 case.
- `decide` confirms that `cycleGraph 6` has 6 edges, is 2-regular and has the expected adjacencies, and that `cycleGraph 8` has 8 edges.
- Every graph on fewer than 6 vertices is `(cycleGraph 6).Free`, and ⊤ on `Fin 6` is not.
- `extremalNumber n (cycleGraph (2k)) ≤ n.choose 2`, so no junk value is reachable.

The statement is neither trivially true nor trivially false: easy C_{2k}-free graphs have only linearly many edges; Bondy–Simonovits gives an O(k n^{1+1/k}) upper bound; the best general lower bound (Lazebnik–Ustimenko–Woldar) has a smaller exponent for k = 4 and k ≥ 6. The `research open` tag matches the source (erdosproblems.com: OPEN, page last edited 18 January 2026; the teorth database also says open). The TODO about variants (Benson's k = 3, 5 cases, the Bondy–Simonovits upper bound) is an omission, not a misformalization.
